question.problem:
Which of the following completes the statement so that it is true:

*If $det[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\ne 0$, then $\text{__________}$ . *

I. The lines $ax+by=0$ and $cx+dy=0$ don't intersect

II. The lines $ax+by=0$ and $cx+dy=0$ intersect at infinitely many points

III. The system $[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]x=0$ has the unique zero solution.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that given $A=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}]$, then according to the invertible matrix theorem the following statements are equivalent:    

1\. $A$ is invertible.

2\. The system $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b.$

3\. The system $Ax=0$ has the unique zero solution.

4\. The lines ${a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1}$ and ${a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2}$ intersect at exactly one point.

5\. $det(A)\ne 0.$

With that in mind, let's now check our statements.

Now, since the fifth part of the invertible matrix theorem is true ($det(A)\ne 0$), all the other parts of the theorem are true too. Therefore, according to the theorem, only option III gives us a true statement: 

*If $det[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\ne 0$, then the system $[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]x=0$ has the unique zero solution.* $\,✓$
